name: SpaceX reusable launch stack
description: SpaceX-centered reusable orbital launch capability map. Falcon 9 and Starship/Super Heavy are separated as product branches; Dragon, Starlink service, Falcon Heavy, and payload customer products are intentionally excluded from the product boundary.

targetContext.targetScale: repeatable orbital launch and recovery across Falcon 9 operations plus Starship/Super Heavy development
targetContext.targetPerformance: launch cadence, booster reuse, safe recovery, rapid refurbishment, payload mass-to-orbit, and cost-per-kg reduction
targetContext.targetUseCase: commercial, government, and internal SpaceX orbital logistics
targetContext.targetEnvironment: US launch/reentry licensing, ocean/RTLS recovery operations, and high-cadence launch sites

name: Reusable orbital launch capability
description: Demand-side capability: move payload mass to orbit with reusable launch hardware, high cadence, controlled recovery, and bounded refurbishment cost.

name: Falcon 9 reusable branch
description: Operational Falcon 9 reuse route centered on first-stage recovery, Merlin reuse, fault-tolerant avionics, fairing recovery, and post-flight refurbishment.

name: Starship / Super Heavy reusable branch
description: Development route for a fully reusable Starship upper stage and reusable Super Heavy booster, with much larger payload capacity but unresolved rapid-reuse, heat-shield, tower-catch, and licensing constraints.

name: Common reuse enablers
description: Shared reuse layer across SpaceX vehicles: health monitoring, engine life margin, flight safety, propellant operations, acceptance testing, and recovery operations.

name: Launch and ground operations stack
description: Ground-side infrastructure and process layer for high-cadence reusable launch: tower systems, propellant loading, pad turnaround, static-fire acceptance, and range coordination.

name: Falcon 9 booster reuse stack
description: First-stage branch covering booster propulsion, structure, reentry control, landing hardware, recovery operations, and refurbishment.

name: Falcon 9 Merlin engine cluster
description: Nine-engine Merlin first-stage propulsion cluster; reuse economics depend on engine life margin, inspection time, and acceptance test yield.

name: Merlin reuse qualification
description: Reuse acceptance logic for engine inspections, trend data, hot-fire margins, and flight readiness after recovery.

name: Merlin turbopump reuse inspection
description: Inspection and trend-screening of turbomachinery after recovery; public details are thin, so this remains a frontier branch.

name: Merlin chamber and nozzle life margin
description: Thermal and structural life-margin model for repeated engine starts, ascent load, entry burn, and landing burn.

name: Falcon 9 aluminum-lithium tank structure
description: Reusable stage structure and tank system; repeated loads and landing environments make structural inspection and fatigue margin relevant.

name: Falcon 9 stage fatigue life
description: Fatigue tracking for recovered stages across ascent, reentry, landing, transport, and relaunch cycles.

name: Falcon 9 grid-fin reentry control
description: Deployable grid fins used to steer the returning booster during atmospheric reentry toward a landing zone or droneship.

name: Falcon 9 landing legs
description: Deployable first-stage landing legs for vertical recovery; a mature subsystem but still part of the recovery reliability chain.

name: Falcon 9 boostback, entry, and landing burns
description: Guidance and propellant allocation across recovery burns; directly controls recovery success and payload performance tradeoffs.

name: Falcon 9 landing propellant margin
description: Mission-design tradeoff between payload delivery and reserve propellant for boostback, entry, and landing burns.

name: Falcon 9 droneship / RTLS recovery ops
description: Operational workflow for autonomous spaceport droneship or return-to-launch-site recovery, safing, transport, and reuse handoff.

name: Falcon 9 post-flight inspection and refurbishment
description: Turnaround process after booster recovery; bottleneck is time, inspection confidence, replacement scope, and acceptance testing before reflight.

name: Falcon 9 second-stage payload delivery
description: Expendable upper-stage delivery layer. It is not the reusable hardware itself, but it affects Falcon 9 mission envelope and launch economics.

name: Merlin Vacuum upper-stage engine
description: Single Merlin Vacuum engine on Falcon upper stage; payload guide notes the fixed nozzle and upper-stage role.

name: Falcon 9 fault-tolerant avionics and GNC
description: Fault-tolerant avionics and guidance, navigation, and control layer with single-fault tolerance and redundant/triplicated elements according to the payload guide.

name: Falcon 9 pneumatic stage separation
description: Low-shock separation subsystem documented in the Falcon payload guide; important because separation reliability affects mission and reuse safety.

name: Falcon 9 fairing recovery and reuse
description: Payload-fairing recovery and reuse branch; economically relevant but separate from first-stage reuse.

name: Starship / Super Heavy vehicle stack
description: Integrated booster and ship architecture for the Starship route.

name: Super Heavy reusable booster
description: Reusable first-stage booster branch for Starship/Super Heavy, including Raptor cluster, boostback, grid fins, and catch interface.

name: Super Heavy 33-Raptor engine cluster
description: Large clustered methalox propulsion layer for Super Heavy; a key integration bottleneck for reliability, throttling, and reuse.

name: Raptor methalox staged-combustion engine
description: Reusable methane/oxygen engine family used on Starship and Super Heavy; engine reliability and reuse margin are central to the route.

name: Raptor clean reuse margin
description: Engine-health and combustion-stability margin needed for repeated launch, landing, and relaunch cycles.

name: Subcooled methane / oxygen propellant ops
description: Ground loading, densification, boiloff control, and engine feed operations for subcooled liquid methane and oxygen.

name: Super Heavy grid-fin control
description: Grid-fin and control-surface layer for Super Heavy return and catch profiles.

name: Super Heavy tower-catch interface
description: Launch tower catch interface. This is a high-leverage Starship reuse bottleneck because it replaces landing legs with site-specific infrastructure and precision approach logic.

name: Super Heavy RTLS boostback profile
description: Return-to-launch-site mission design and control method for Super Heavy recovery.

name: Starship reusable ship upper stage
description: Reusable upper-stage/spacecraft branch for orbital delivery and return.

name: Starship sea-level and vacuum Raptor mix
description: Ship propulsion mix of sea-level and vacuum-optimized Raptor engines, per 2026 filing descriptions.

name: Starship heat-shield tile system
description: Reusable thermal-protection layer for ship reentry; tile durability, attachment, inspection, and replacement time are central bottlenecks.

name: Starship tile bonding and inspection process
description: Tile attachment, inspection, replacement, and acceptance process after heating and vibration cycles.

name: Starship stainless-steel primary structure
description: Stainless-steel structure selected for Starship-class thermal and manufacturing tradeoffs; exact alloy/process details remain outside this first pass.

name: Starship flap reentry control
description: Ship flaps and control method for atmospheric reentry, attitude control, and landing transition.

name: Starship orbital payload deployment bay
description: Payload accommodation and deployment branch for high-mass Starship missions.

name: Starship reentry and landing burn profile
description: Flight-control method for ship reentry, flip, engine relight, and terminal landing burn.

name: Integrated launch tower and chopsticks
description: Launch, stacking, and catch infrastructure for Starship/Super Heavy; makes reuse dependent on ground-site precision and uptime.

name: Methane / oxygen ground propellant system
description: Storage, loading, chilldown, and tank farm operations for high-cadence methalox launch.

name: Launch-pad rapid turnaround process
description: Pad inspection, repair, propellant reset, range readiness, and vehicle integration process between launches.

name: Vehicle health monitoring telemetry
description: Flight and ground telemetry pipeline used to decide whether recovered hardware can fly again.

name: Reuse acceptance and static-fire process
description: Test and acceptance workflow after assembly or refurbishment, including static-fire logic where required.

name: Autonomous flight safety system
description: Flight safety system layer that bounds public-safety risk during launch and recovery operations.

name: Range safety and airspace coordination
description: Coordination of hazard areas, launch windows, NOTAMs, range assets, and recovery zones for high-cadence operations.

name: Cryogenic ground loading sequence
description: Sequencing, chilldown, propellant conditioning, hold logic, and abort recovery for cryogenic launch operations.

name: Methalox engine test stands
description: Ground test infrastructure for Raptor qualification, acceptance, anomaly reproduction, and reuse margin learning.

name: FAA launch and reentry cadence license
description: Regulatory cadence constraint for SpaceX launch and reentry activity. For Starship/Super Heavy Boca Chica, the FAA page references proposed authorization for up to 25 annual orbital launches and landings.

name: Reusable launch cost per kg
description: Investor-facing metric for whether reuse translates into payload-mass economics, not just recovery spectacle.

name: Booster reflight count
description: Observed booster reuse depth; SpaceX 2026 filing language is evidence for high repeat use but still requires independent operational audit.

name: Launch cadence
description: Cadence metric linking vehicle reuse, pad turnaround, regulatory approval, and demand backlog.

name: SpaceX orbital data center system
description: SpaceX-centered preview map for an orbital AI compute / data-center system. Public evidence supports an FCC application and investor-facing intent, but not a mature commercial service; the route is modeled as a future paid-candidate research map, not an already proven product.

targetContext.targetScale: large NGSO constellation of compute satellites if authorized and economically feasible
targetContext.targetPerformance: compute power in orbit, thermal rejection, optical backhaul, radiation resilience, safe constellation operations, and launch cost per useful kW
targetContext.targetUseCase: AI training/inference and data-center workloads using orbital solar power and Starlink-style optical networking
targetContext.targetEnvironment: LEO/NGSO orbital shells, FCC/space-debris constraints, high-radiation/high-vacuum thermal environment

name: Orbital AI compute capability
description: Demand-side capability: deliver useful AI compute from orbit with reliable power, cooling, communication, fault tolerance, and regulatory compliance.

name: Orbital compute payload stack
description: Compute payload branch: accelerators, memory, storage, management, redundancy, software orchestration, and radiation/fault mitigation.

name: Orbital AI accelerator payload racks
description: High-power accelerator payload hardware adapted for launch loads, vacuum, radiation, power cycling, and remote operation.

name: Radiation-tolerant compute board
description: Board-level compute design with shielding, redundancy, power integrity, thermal conduction, and fault recovery.

name: GPU / CPU payload qualification
description: Screening, burn-in, thermal-vacuum, radiation, and fault-injection qualification for high-power AI compute payloads.

name: Fault-tolerant orbital job orchestration
description: Distributed scheduler and recovery method for compute jobs under node resets, radiation upsets, link outages, and orbital handoffs.

name: Orbital ECC memory and storage
description: Memory/storage branch for radiation-induced bit errors, restart recovery, local caching, and data integrity.

name: Onboard secure management plane
description: Remote update, key management, workload isolation, telemetry, and recovery controls for an unmanned orbital data center.

name: Orbital AI workload partitioning
description: Method for splitting training/inference workloads across intermittently connected orbital nodes with bounded latency and failure recovery.

name: Orbital compute firmware update process
description: Remote firmware/driver update, rollback, and recovery workflow for compute payloads that cannot be physically serviced often.

name: Spacecraft bus platform for compute
description: Satellite bus layer providing structure, power, thermal interfaces, attitude control, communications, propulsion, and operations services for compute payloads.

name: Deployable solar power system
description: Solar-array branch for orbital compute power generation. High useful compute kW requires large deployed area, pointing, degradation management, and packaging.

name: High-power solar array packaging
description: Packaging and deployment hardware for large solar arrays compatible with launch volume, loads, and high-volume satellite production.

name: Battery storage and power conditioning
description: Energy storage and conditioning layer for eclipse operations, peak compute loads, battery life, and power quality.

name: Rad-hard power distribution unit
description: Power distribution and protection electronics for high-power payloads in a radiation environment.

name: Eclipse power budget management
description: Scheduling and throttling method for orbital day/night cycles, battery state, thermal limits, and link availability.

name: Orbital energy-aware scheduler
description: Compute scheduler that turns orbital power/thermal states into workload placement and throttling decisions.

name: Orbital thermal rejection stack
description: Thermal branch for removing high compute heat in vacuum. This is the clearest first-order bottleneck because waste heat can only be moved and radiated, not convected away.

name: Deployable radiator panels
description: Deployable radiators for high-power heat rejection; radiator area, deployment reliability, pointing, and degradation set useful compute density.

name: Heat-pipe / loop-heat-pipe network
description: Heat transport layer from accelerator payloads to radiator surfaces; failure modes include dryout, interface resistance, deployment motion, and thermal cycling.

name: Compute cold plate and fluid loop
description: Cold plates or fluid-loop elements that collect heat from dense accelerator payloads and move it toward radiators.

name: Radiator surface coatings and degradation
description: Radiator optical coatings and surface materials whose absorptivity/emissivity change under UV, atomic oxygen, and particle exposure.

name: Thermal modeling and control algorithm
description: Model predictive thermal control tying payload throttling, radiator attitude, orbital heating, and fault states together.

name: Optical ISL network fabric
description: High-bandwidth optical inter-satellite link network layer for compute satellites; FCC notice says the proposed system would primarily rely on optical ISLs and connect with Starlink systems.

name: Starlink laser-terminal backhaul
description: Laser-terminal and optical-backhaul layer; relevant because the FCC notice ties the data-center system to SpaceX first- and second-generation Starlink systems.

name: Optical pointing, acquisition, and tracking
description: PAT control required to keep high-rate laser links aligned across moving spacecraft.

name: Mesh routing and congestion control
description: Routing and load-balancing method for orbital mesh traffic between compute nodes, Starlink links, and ground gateways.

name: TT&C and ground-link layer
description: Telemetry, tracking, command, and ground-link operations layer; FCC notice identifies TT&C operations in the proposed system.

name: Starlink interconnect gateway
description: Gateway layer connecting orbital compute traffic to Starlink's broader network and ground users where authorized.

name: Radiation environment mitigation
description: Mitigation branch for total ionizing dose, single-event effects, solar activity, shielding, parts selection, and software recovery.

name: TID shielding and layout
description: Shielding, layout, and material strategy to keep electronics within mission radiation limits.

name: SEE watchdog and recovery
description: Detection and recovery for single-event upset/latchup/fault states affecting compute and power electronics.

name: COTS part screening and upscreening
description: Part selection, screening, derating, and lot control for non-traditional high-performance compute electronics in space.

name: Orbital deployment launch stack
description: Launch and deployment branch for compute satellites: upmass, payload integration, deployment interfaces, orbital shell insertion, and cadence.

name: Starship mass-to-orbit enabler
description: Heavy-lift economic enabler for orbital compute deployment; this is a dependency, not the data-center product itself.

name: Compute-satellite deployment interface
description: Mechanical/electrical launch accommodation and separation interface for large compute satellites.

name: Orbital shell constellation operations
description: Fleet operations for many compute satellites across orbital shells, handoffs, health checks, and capacity management.

name: Collision avoidance and deorbit compliance
description: Autonomous conjunction screening, maneuver planning, end-of-life disposal, and debris-risk management for a large NGSO compute constellation.

name: Space environment regulatory license
description: Authorization and waiver layer for SpaceX's proposed Orbital Data Center system; currently public-notice stage, not commercial deployment.

name: Manufacturing and qualification stack
description: Factory, test, and qualification branch for high-volume compute satellites.

name: Thermal-vacuum test campaign
description: TVAC test process for compute payload, power, thermal rejection, and software throttling across mission thermal states.

name: Radiation test campaign
description: Test campaign for TID, SEE, latchup, reset behavior, and data integrity under expected orbit environment.

name: Vibration and launch-load test
description: Mechanical test branch for high-mass/high-power compute payloads and deployable power/thermal hardware.

name: High-volume compute satellite factory line
description: Factory process for producing compute satellites at meaningful scale; public evidence is currently too thin for capacity claims.

name: Space-grade connector supply
description: Connector and interconnect branch for high-reliability space electronics; supplier identity needs a separate audit before gating claims are promoted.

name: Vacuum-compatible compute harness
description: Harnessing, shielding, grounding, and thermal/mechanical interface branch for dense compute payloads.

name: Orbital compute ground segment integration
description: Ground software, gateway, customer API, billing, and operations integration needed to turn satellites into a usable compute service.

name: In-orbit serviceability and recovery strategy
description: Strategy for failed payload isolation, degraded-mode operation, software recovery, replacement launch, and disposal when physical service is limited.

name: Orbital compute business-model validation
description: Customer, latency, reliability, insurance, utilization, launch cost, and terrestrial competition assumptions that decide whether orbital compute becomes economic.

name: Compute power per satellite
description: Useful compute kW per satellite after power, thermal, radiation, and duty-cycle limits. Public SpaceX system-level claims need review before values are used.

metrics.name: Current audited value
metrics.description: Blocking commercial unknown: without a reviewed useful-kW value, orbital compute economics cannot be priced.

name: Orbital network latency and bandwidth
description: Bandwidth and latency between compute satellites, Starlink links, gateways, and customers.

name: Orbital thermal dissipation margin
description: Thermal margin after waste heat, radiator area, orbital heating, coating degradation, and throttling.

name: Launch cost per useful compute kW
description: Economic metric linking Starship/Falcon launch cost, payload lifetime, power generation, thermal throttling, utilization, and replacement cadence.

metrics.name: Current audited value
metrics.description: Blocking commercial unknown: this value must combine launch price, payload lifetime, utilization, power, and thermal throttling before the map can support paid exposure.

name: SpaceX
description: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. is the product owner/operator in both SpaceX-centered maps. The owner identity is visible as route context; public filing sources in this first pass are treated only as listing-context research inputs, and no active ticker or public listing is promoted until human review confirms it.

name: Rocket Lab
description: Public space company with launch and space-systems exposure. Included as comparable/supplier capability exposure, not as a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: Redwire
description: Public space infrastructure company. Included as a public exposure candidate for spacecraft components and thermal/deployable systems, not as a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: L3Harris Technologies
description: Public aerospace/defense company with space and optical communications capabilities. Included as capability exposure, not as a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: Honeywell Aerospace
description: Honeywell space electronics and avionics capability exposure. Included as a public supplier candidate, not as a confirmed SpaceX orbital data-center BOM item.

name: RTX / Blue Canyon Technologies
description: RTX subsidiary Blue Canyon Technologies supplies spacecraft buses and mission operations capabilities. Included as public bus/platform exposure, not as confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: Launch-customer exposure research placeholder
description: Placeholder for future demand-side analysis of public companies relying on SpaceX launch services. It is deliberately not connected as supplier exposure until a dedicated customer/demand relation exists.
